issues.description: The problem statement UML specifies singFarmSongVerse as a private method (negative visibility), while the template Farm.java declares a private method stub with no parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)) and the solution implements it as protected (protected void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)). This visibility difference between the UML/problem, the template stub, and the solution can confuse students about the intended access level for the helper method and whether it should accept an Animal parameter. It may also cause questions about whether tests or other classes should be able to call or override this method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent across artifacts. Either: (a) update the solution to match the UML/template by declaring the helper as private and including the Animal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) or (b) update the UML and template to indicate protected if the method is intentionally meant to be accessible to subclasses. Also update the template method signature to include the Animal parameter so students implement the method with the correct signature.
